title: Roofline time bound
caption: A kernel's time is bounded by the worse of its compute term and its memory term. Below the ridge intensity the bandwidth term governs — the nameplate rate is unreachable no matter how the kernel is tuned.

title: Ridge-point intensity
caption: The arithmetic intensity where compute time and memory time balance. Workloads below I* are memory-bound; above it, compute-bound. Compute growing 18× against bandwidth's 8.9× pushes the ridge right each generation — the same part needs ~2× the intensity to stay fed.

symbols.meaning: ridge intensity in FLOP per byte — the compute/memory crossover
peak compute rate, e.g. ~989 TFLOP/s dense FP16 on H100
memory bandwidth, e.g. 3.35 TB/s HBM3 on H100

title: Decode latency floor
caption: At batch 1 every token re-reads all weights, so the floor is weight bytes divided by bandwidth. A 2 TB model: ~250 ms/token on ~8 TB/s HBM3, ~125 ms on HBM4. FLOPs never enter the formula — the opening question's answer.

symbols.meaning: weight bytes read per token (full model at batch 1)

title: Static training state
caption: FP16 weights (2 B/param) + FP16 gradients (2 B/param) + FP32 optimizer moments and master weights (~8 B/param): ~12 bytes per parameter before activations. 175B params → ~2.1 TB against 640 GiB of node HBM — sharding is mandatory, and the optimizer term dominates.

symbols.meaning: resident bytes of training state, excluding activations

title: Sustained GPU-hours
caption: Peak-rate estimates are optimistic by 1/MFU. A job quoted at 1,000 GPU-hours from the nameplate books 2,500 real hours at MFU 0.4 — before a single interruption. Plans priced at peak under-budget the run.

symbols.meaning: GPU-hours the schedule must actually reserve
GPU-hours implied by dividing work by peak rate
model FLOPs usage: achieved rate ÷ nameplate

title: Composite node failure rate
caption: Every component in the node — GPU, CPU, NIC, drive, PSU — adds its own failure rate. An eight-GPU node interrupts more often than any part inside it, which is why health monitoring and replacement run at node granularity and why the pod composes to a ~5 h job MTBF.

symbols.meaning: node-level failure rate, the sum of component rates
